name: Ash, cow dung or heat on the baby's umbilical cord
what_people_do: Birth attendants and relatives cut the cord with a razor blade and dress the stump with ash, cow dung or a hot compress.
why_they_say_it_works: To dry the stump quickly and prevent bleeding or "spirits".

documented_by.source: Umbilical cord care practices, Sokoto and Bauchi, Nigeria, 2017, BMC Pregnancy Childbirth, PMID 29121870
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Bauchi and Sokoto, Nigeria, about 1,140 and 1,311 households per round: over 75% and over 80% of cords cut with razor blades; traditional birth attendants kept using ash, cow dung and hot compress; chlorhexidine gel uptake rose in facilities.

evidence.finding: Authors state that neonatal infections from unsafe cord practices account for the majority of neonatal deaths in Nigeria and call these practices unsafe.

source.name: Umbilical cord care practices, Sokoto and Bauchi, Nigeria, 2017, BMC Pregnancy Childbirth, PMID 29121870

harm_note: Ash and dung on a cord stump are linked by the authors to fatal infection; chlorhexidine gel is the replacement.
gaps: Death attribution is the authors' statement; not independently checked.
